question: In a paediatric resuscitation scenario, peripheral IV cannulation should be abandoned and intraosseous access established if two IV attempts fail within 90 seconds.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The 90-second / 2-attempt threshold is standard guidance in paediatric resuscitation (PALS and IAP guidelines). Prolonged attempts at peripheral IV in a compromised child waste critical time. IO access provides equivalent drug delivery to IV and should not be seen as a last resort — it is the planned next step after 2 failed IV attempts.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In any paediatric life-threatening emergency, the 90-second / 2-attempt rule applies: if two peripheral IV attempts fail or 90 seconds elapse without successful access, proceed immediately to IO insertion. Delay in vascular access directly increases morbidity and mortality in paediatric cardiac arrest.
